$comment: Single source of truth for which paths belong to Trellis rather than to your project. Read by the map generator, the linter configs in setup/, and the integrity check. Add to this rather than repeating the list anywhere else.
$note: trellis.json is listed because it is Trellis's own declaration format, even though its contents are yours. Your project's source, tests, docs/specs and docs/mockups are never framework-owned.
$requiredIgnoresNote: Lines Trellis owns inside .gitignore, which it does NOT own as a file — projects add their own entries, so it cannot be replaced wholesale. trellis-update.sh appends any that are missing. This is not cosmetic: Trellis writes runtime state into .claude/ (the gate lock, verify state), and both run-spec.sh and deliver-run.sh refuse to work on a dirty tree — so an unignored lock file made delivery refuse whenever a gate run was in flight. The pattern rather than a list of names, because the previous entry named .verify-state.json alone and the gate lock arrived later.
$lintNote: Trellis ships scripts in Python and bash. A project that adds a linter would otherwise fail its very first lint run on files it does not own and cannot reasonably be asked to fix. setup/ ships ready-made exclusion configs for common linters.
$generatedNote: Files Trellis writes rather than people. They conflict on every concurrent branch and the conflict is never meaningful, because there is a canonical resolution: regenerate. .gitattributes routes them to a merge driver that does exactly that. check-integrity asserts this list and .gitattributes agree, so adding a generated file without an entry is caught rather than discovered during a merge.
$ownedNote: Directories rather than files, deliberately. An earlier hand-written list of individual files omitted .claude/lib/frontmatter.py, and anyone following it got an integrity check that died with ModuleNotFoundError. A directory cannot omit a file added inside it. This list is what trellis-update.sh copies, so it is load-bearing rather than documentation.
$trellisJsonNote: trellis.json is listed because Trellis defines its FORMAT, but its CONTENTS belong to the project. trellis-update.sh never overwrites it.
